opex.note: Developing new medicines — up 26% as the pipeline widened.

opex.name: Marketing, selling & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and running the company — up 29% to support new launches.

opex.name: Acquired IPR&D
opex.note: Research bought in from other companies, expensed on the spot.

opex.name: Asset impairment & restructuring
opex.note: Write-downs and reorganization costs — well down from $344M a year ago.

follow100Note: Mounjaro and Zepbound together supplied $60.49 of every $100 Lilly took in — two versions of the same drug, tirzepatide, now drive three-fifths of the company.
footerNote: Reported (GAAP) figures throughout; Lilly's non-GAAP net income was $6,771M (EPS $7.54).
oneTimers: Acquired IPR&D of $529M ($0.52 per share): Lilly expensed research it bought from other companies. It is a recurring feature of Lilly's deal-making, but the size swings from quarter to quarter.

The year-ago quarter included a one-time $300M Jardiance benefit from an amended collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim, which makes this quarter's growth in the older medicines look worse than it was.
otherDetail: Net other expense of $108M — interest costs of $123M, partly covered by $15M of other income.

segments.name: Mounjaro
segments.note: The diabetes shot — $4.1B in the U.S. and $3.3B overseas as launches rolled out worldwide.

segments.name: Zepbound
segments.note: The obesity shot — sold in the U.S., Canada and Japan, and still growing fast.

segments.name: All other medicines
segments.note: Everything else Lilly sells, led by Verzenio at $1.6B — down as a group because a one-time $300M Jardiance benefit flattered last year's quarter.

takeaways.text: Mounjaro ($7.4B, +110%) and Zepbound ($4.3B, +123%) — both are tirzepatide — together brought in $11.7B of the $19.3B total. Company-wide volume rose 46%, partly offset by prices 5% lower.
takeaways.title: One drug, three-fifths of sales

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 63% to $8.4B. An 82.5% gross margin means most of each new sales dollar survives — and Lilly reinvested some of it in research (+26%) and launch marketing (+29%).
takeaways.title: Profits grew faster than sales

takeaways.text: Lilly guided 2026 revenue to $80–83B, up from $65.2B in 2025, with non-GAAP EPS of $33.50–35.00 — betting that new factory capacity and the orforglipron pill keep the growth going.
takeaways.title: 2026 guided even bigger

verdict: Lilly's revenue jumped 43% to $19.3B as Mounjaro and Zepbound sales more than doubled — and profit rose 50% to $6.6B, even with $529M spent buying in outside research.
